ask: Which issues should we make for building a template as people go?
problem: Some teams do not know their template before they start. They want to divide books, or add books, folders and stories, while they translate.
found: I could not test on a phone or in the browser. The local sign-up service would not start here, because it could not reach its packages. So this comes from the code and the app's own test steps. Dividing a book works. Team leads and admins tap a waiting book, tap Divide, and divide it their own way: tap a verse to start a section, name it, undo it. Translators see only a note that the coordinator decides. Adding books, folders or stories works only in the template editor under Manage. The map and passage screens have no way to add them, so a person must stop translating and go find the template.
changed: Nothing yet. No code changed. This card only holds pictures and a question.
why: You asked for a walk-through and a question before anything is built. I looked at the map, the book page, the divide screens, the template editor and the flow map in the code.
touches: Nothing today. Option 2 would change who may edit the organization's templates.

pictures.label: Adding books, folders and stories today

options.label: Make two issues: add parts from the map
options.result: One issue adds a folder or story from the map of an outline language. One adds a missing book from the map of a Bible language. Dividing stays as it is.

options.label: Make three issues: also let language leads divide
options.result: The two issues above, plus one so language leads can divide waiting books. This changes who may edit templates, so it needs a choice first.

options.label: Make no issues until you test on a phone
options.result: Nothing is built. You walk both flows on a phone and write here what felt slow or hard.
